vulnerabilities.description: packages/graph-core/src/eap/capabilities.ts:143 validateOperatorApproval compares `approval.basedOnSeq !== currentSeq`, where `currentSeq` is read verbatim from the caller-supplied CapabilityExecutionRequest (capability-gateway.ts:135 forwards `{...request, approval: storedApproval}`). Retry #5 correctly moved scope, expiry and basedOnSeq to the STORED grant so the request can no longer define them - but it left the OTHER side of the same comparison caller-controlled, so the APPROVAL_STALE_SEQ control is inert. Reproduced: registered approval 'apS' with basedOnSeq 99 against a tenant whose real horizon seq is 0, then called capabilities.execute with `currentSeq: 99` and `approval: {id:'apS'}`; result was {status:'COMPLETED'}, provider invoked once, irreversible grant consumed. Any holder of an unconsumed, unexpired, in-scope approval can replay it against arbitrary world state by asserting the sequence the approval was bound to. Violates test-scenarios 1.2 'Should reject Operator Approval when scope, expiry, or Sequence does not match' and 3.2 'Should refuse stale or out-of-scope Operator Approval'. The gateway must resolve the current sequence from the durable horizon/ledger itself, exactly as it already resolves the approval. NOTE ON REACH: no cognitive.* tool routes to the gateway, so this is not remotely reachable today - it is reachable through the documented library surface startServer().eap(tenantId).capabilities.execute(), which is the surface an embedding host is meant to drive with agent input. Rated per the authorization-control severity floor.

Recall now genuinely traverses, degrades and scars (the LOW finding about eapRecall doing nothing is CLOSED), but the degradation is never applied to the authoritative knowledge tables, so no other code path can observe it. Reproduced end-to-end through MCP: advance candidate 'k1' to 'admitted' in h1, cognitive.contest(invalidating) -> admitted, cognitive.recall -> ok:true with degradedClaims [{claimId:'k1', previousState:'admitted', newState:'recalled'}]. Immediately afterwards `SELECT state FROM candidates WHERE candidate_id='k1'` still returns 'admitted'; cognitive.propose CONCRETIZE on k1 returns ok:true and advances it to 'concretized'; cognitive.contest on k1 still resolves it as admitted knowledge. The 'recalled' state exists only inside the recall_cases.state JSON blob, which only SqliteRecallRepository reads. Consequence: knowledge invalidated by an admitted invalidating contestation stays admitted, keeps climbing the lifecycle, and can be VERIFYed and promoted into a parent horizon. Test-scenarios 1.1 Recall Case (degrade the normatively resolved affected claims) and 3.1 'Should execute resumable Recall' are only half met. Held at MEDIUM rather than HIGH deliberately: the degradation IS durably recorded with provenance, the spec (004 line 128) explicitly forbids erasing or directly rewriting the admitted record, and 003 defers the destination status of indirect dependents - what is missing is a read-side consumer of recall state on the lifecycle and promotion gates, not a rewrite.

packages/mcp-server/src/tools/eap.ts:205 (and :309 for promote) the optimistic-concurrency gate is `if (args.basedOnSeq < horizon.seq) -> STALE_BASE`, with the only upper-bound validation being Number.isInteger. Number.isInteger(1e308) is true, so any inflated value passes the rebase gate unconditionally and forever. Reproduced through MCP: horizon 'hb' at seq 2, cognitive.propose with basedOnSeq 1e308 returned ok:true and advanced the candidate to 'concretized' at seq 3, while a legitimate basedOnSeq 1 on the same horizon was correctly refused with STALE_BASE. A client that always sends a large basedOnSeq is never subject to the freshness check at all - the guard is opt-in from the caller's side. Two defects compound: no MAX bound (test-scenarios 3.3 'Should reject oversized or out-of-range contract values', which is enforced for strings via MAX_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH but not for numbers), and a `<` comparison where the contract wants equality with the observed sequence - a caller claiming to be based on a FUTURE sequence is admitted as fresh.

The Horizon Budget Ledger is still stored and never enforced - unchanged from the previous verdict, and openly declared open by the implementer. tools/eap.ts:107 writes budget_allocated on eapInitiate; nothing anywhere increments budget_consumed or compares the two. HorizonStore.saveTransition accepts a budgetConsumed override (horizon-store.ts:124) that no caller passes, and the BudgetLedger / HorizonBudgetExhausted logic in graph-core/src/eap/horizon.ts:80 is wired to nothing on the reachable path. Reproduced: cognitive.initiate with budget {limit:0} followed by DELIBERATE, ADMIT and CONCRETIZE all returned ok:true with the horizons row still at budget_allocated 0 / budget_consumed 0. Test-scenarios 1.1 'Should escalate without promotion when the Horizon budget is exhausted' has no implementation.

Unguarded JSON.parse on stored columns still throws an untyped SyntaxError out of the repository boundary instead of producing a typed Refusal: packages/mcp-server/src/eap/eap-repositories.ts:130 (promotion_events payload), :139 (proposal candidates), :186-187 (contestation target_claim_ids/evidence), :342-350 (recall checkpoint/state/notice/closure), :365 (scar), :652 (audit outcome). Re-reproduced on current HEAD: saved contestation 'ct1', corrupted target_claim_ids to '{not json', SqliteContestationRepository.get threw SyntaxError 'JSON Parse error: Expected }'. Unreachable from client input today because every writer stringifies, but rebuildFromJsonl replays arbitrary on-disk JSONL into exactly these columns, so a truncated or hand-edited mirror turns a governed read into an unhandled crash rather than a refusal (test-scenarios 2.1, durable rebuild).

eapPromote is still not idempotent and has no in-flight guard. Reproduced through MCP: candidate 'c3' VERIFYed in horizon 'child', then two identical cognitive.promote calls both returned ok:true, minting proposals prop-prom-child-root-...-5umry and ...-272jy and burning child-horizon sequences 7 and 8. The duplicate-candidate write into the parent is guarded (tools/eap.ts:401 `if (existing) continue`), so no state is corrupted, but the parent gate now has two competing proposals for the same distillation and the child's sequence advanced twice for one epistemic act. Compare eapRecall, which is explicitly idempotent by contestation id (verified: replay returned the same recall case with replayed:true and no second degradation).

edgeCasesMissed: RE-VERIFIED CLOSED, recorded for the log: (1) SqliteApprovalRepository.registerApproval is create-only - register/consume/consume/re-register/consume now yields registered:false 'already registered and has been consumed' and the third consume is still APPROVAL_ALREADY_USED; a spent grant cannot be re-armed. (2) resolveExpiry fails closed - registering expiresAt 'not-a-date' is refused at registration, and an expiry corrupted directly in the column yields APPROVAL_EXPIRED with 0 provider calls. (3) Idempotency is reserved before the provider call - three concurrent execute() calls with key 'SAME' produced exactly 1 provider invocation, 1 COMPLETED and 2 REFUSED/IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and a later replay returned isCached:true with still 1 invocation. (4) SqliteRecallRepository.complete() without a case survives rebuildFromJsonl - status stays 'completed' after replay. (5) eapContest refuses [null] and ['   '] evidence with EVIDENCE_REQUIRED and refuses path-traversal / cross-tenant targets with RESOURCE_ABSENT; status is no longer hard-coded. (6) eapPromote refuses a candidate absent from the child (RESOURCE_ABSENT) and one that is merely 'admitted' (ILLEGAL_TRANSITION). (7) eapRecall drives the real RecallWorker, is replay-idempotent, and refuses a non-invalidating contestation with RECALL_UNPROVEN.

Capability execution and persistent-delta admission ARE now reachable and governed, but only as a library surface: startServer().eap(tenantId) returns the composition root and .capabilities.execute() enforced approval single-use across two different idempotency keys (second call REFUSED APPROVAL_ALREADY_USED), while getAuditLog({principal:'p',scopes:[]}) correctly returned the redacted projection. .admitPersistentDelta refused a malformed envelope with a typed reason list. Residual gap: transport.ts still registers only cognitive.initiate/propose/promote/contest/recall, so test-scenarios 3.1 'irreversible Capability through the MCP boundary' and 2.3 idempotency reconciliation remain unexercised over JSON-RPC. 003 declares no tool surface for them, so this is a spec/transport alignment question rather than a defect - but it also means the currentSeq flaw above sits on the only surface a host would use.

eapContest silently DISCARDS non-string evidence elements instead of refusing the contract: `args.evidence.filter(ref => typeof ref === 'string')` at tools/eap.ts:492 means evidence [{a:1},'ok-ev'] is admitted as if one reference had been supplied. Correct outcome for the all-invalid case (refused), but a caller is never told part of its evidence was dropped.

Cross-process / cross-connection concurrency is still unverified. serialTransaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) plus the durable allocator is the right primitive and the in-process race is now genuinely closed for idempotency and approval consumption, but every concurrency test still shares one bun:sqlite handle. No test opens a second connection or a second process, so SQLITE_BUSY handling on the reserve/consume path remains untested - as the implementer states honestly.

packages/client/src/eap.ts:176 still sends `basedOnSeq: input.basedOnSeq ?? 0`. Against any horizon whose seq has advanced this is a value the client knows is stale and the host refuses with STALE_BASE. The adapter should omit the field rather than fabricate 0. (Ironically the host's missing upper bound means the client's own workaround would be to send a huge number - see the basedOnSeq finding.)

promotion_events is read whole: SqlitePromotionRepository.getEvents() at eap-repositories.ts:126 does `SELECT payload ... ORDER BY ordinal` with no LIMIT/OFFSET and JSON.parses every row into memory. Unbounded append-only table, unbounded read. Not a correctness defect today; it is the one remaining unbounded accumulator after the capability-audit retention policy closed the other.

Test-scenarios 1.1 Horizon 'Should retain horizon-local authority when assignment to another Horizon is attempted': still no code path refuses an attempt to assign Relative Authority across horizons. Promotion correctly enters every candidate at 'proposed' in the parent (verified), so authority is not inherited - but the explicit refusal the scenario asks for does not exist.
